construction: (a) Loss-series block bootstrap, plain SE, full-scale adjustment
mechanism: Resamples the loss series only; parameter-estimation error is a per-history common shock invisible to any reshuffling of the differentials.
HAC absorbs serial dependence within a history but not the between-history component arising from parameter estimation, which no resampling of the loss series can reproduce.

construction: (c) Calhoun data-level block bootstrap, HAC statistic
mechanism: Resampling raw data with per-draw refitting recreates estimation error in principle, but chunk-gluing destroys the persistence the estimation step depends on; no block length balances realism against variety.

construction: (d) Model-based null-imposed ARMA bootstrap, HAC statistic
mechanism: Simulating seamless histories from a fitted null generator preserves persistence exactly and imposes the null by construction, so estimation error enters the draw distribution.
